You’re not imagining it—these devices *are* designed to grab your attention. The good news is you can absolutely tame that and make it feel a lot more like a quiet, well-organized workspace instead of a flashing control panel.

Here are the most useful things to adjust, without getting too technical:

First, notifications (this is the big one)  
Go into your tablet’s **Settings**, then look for **Notifications**. You’ll see a list of apps.  
- Tap on apps you don’t care about (games, shopping, news apps you didn’t choose) and turn notifications **off**.  
- For things you *do* want (like messages or email), you can often tone them down—disable sounds or pop-ups but still allow them to appear quietly.

Second, clean up the home screen  
Think of your home screen like your drafting table—only keep what you actually use.  
- Press and hold an app icon, then move it or remove it from the main screen.  
- You can group things into folders (for example: “News,” “Utilities,” “Photos”).  
- Anything you don’t recognize and don’t want—you can usually remove it.

Third, silence interruptions when you want peace  
Look for something called **Do Not Disturb** or **Focus Mode** in Settings.  
- You can turn it on manually when you want quiet time.  
- Or even schedule it (for example, every evening after dinner).

Fourth, tame the news  
If you’re using a news app or the browser:  
- Stick to one or two trusted sources instead of apps that send constant “breaking news” alerts.  
- Many news apps have a setting to turn off “breaking alerts” but still let you read at your own pace.

Fifth, simplify what you see  
Some tablets have a **“Simple mode”** or **“Easy mode”** (often under Display or Accessibility). It makes icons bigger and reduces clutter—worth checking if it’s there.

If you’d like, tell me what kind of tablet it is (iPad, Samsung, something else), and I can give you very exact, step-by-step instructions—like a set of clean blueprints.

You’re approaching this exactly the right way, by the way: strip away the noise and keep only what serves a purpose.
